data.body:
ROUND 4: BLOCK, one finding, ACCEPTED — and it is a trap I had ALREADY been burned by earlier in this session and reintroduced anyway.

AC2(b) required 'a comment on THIS ticket quotes both observed outputs'. A ticket comment lives OUTSIDE the repository, and the completion verifier reads repository files ONLY, so that criterion could never be confirmed from the codebase and would have burned a close cycle. This is the identical mechanism that blocked bug 7cbe's close a few hours ago, where the fix was to tag machine-local criteria [operator-attested]. I learned it there and then wrote the same shape back into this plan while remediating round 3.

REMEDIATED by splitting the criterion along the repo boundary rather than tagging the whole thing:
 - the DOCSTRING half stays untagged and in-repo. That is deliberate: the docstring is the artifact a future reader hits before 'simplifying' the subprocess isolation away, so it must live in the repository where the verifier — and the reader — can see it.
 - the EXPERIMENT half is now [operator-attested], because its evidence is transient command output with no repository artifact and no CI check.

APPLYING LAST ROUND'S LESSON RATHER THAN WAITING TO BE TOLD: I swept ALL criteria for out-of-repo evidence instead of fixing only the cited one. Result: AC3 is the only genuinely out-of-repo criterion and is now tagged. One apparent hit on the 'no production behaviour changes' criterion was a false positive of my own keyword heuristic — it matched the word 'comments' in 'corrects comments only', which is verifiable from the diff. Every other criterion asserts on a test or a repository file.

Round-by-round: (1) a factual error, (2) an unexecutable falsification claim, (3) an under-specified artifact plus a missed sibling, (4) an out-of-repo criterion. Narrowing each time. The recurring cause is asserting rather than checking, and the recurring fix is to run the sweep the finding implies instead of only the edit it names.
